summary: Mizuho Okita works in Indology and religious studies. She earned a BA at Tokai University, studied at Gakushuin University, and studied under Katsuhiko Kamimura and doctoral supervisor Atsuhiko Yoshida. She held a part-time lecturer post at Meisei University in 2008.
Mizumaro Ishida was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Tokai University, attested in 1976 and 1987.
Mohammad Ashraf Dar is a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. In 2014, he was attested as an MPhil student and research scholar at Vikram University.

Mona Schrempf specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. She earned a doctorate in anthropology from the Free University of Berlin by 2001 and held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin and Heidelberg University in 2006.

Monica Esposito was a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. She studied at Ca' Foscari University of Venice and Paris Diderot University (PhD ~1988–1993), and later served as an associate professor at Kyoto University.

Monier Monier-Williams was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Oxford under Horace Hayman Wilson. He taught at East India Company College (~1844–1858) and Cheltenham College (~1858–1860) before serving as Oxford's Boden Professor of Sanskrit from 1860.

Monika Horstmann is an Indology and religious studies scholar. She held posts at the University of Cologne (~1981–1992), ANU, FU Berlin, Bonn, EPHE, and Heidelberg University, where she was attested in 2009 as emeritus professor.

Monika Zin specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. She studied at Jagiellonian University and LMU Munich, later holding professorships at LMU Munich (~2001–2016) and FU Berlin (~2014–2015), and a research leadership post at the Saxon Academy in 2016.

Moriichi Yamazaki is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Cambridge. He held positions at Rissho University (~1982–1986), Sendai College (~1986–2003), and served as president of Hosen Gakuen College (~2004–2014).

Moritz Abraham Stern worked in linguistics and other fields. He studied at Heidelberg University and the University of Göttingen under Carl Friedrich Gauss, subsequently holding an academic post at Göttingen from 1830 to 1884.

Moriz Haupt was a scholar of linguistics who studied at Leipzig University under Gottfried Hermann. He held academic posts at Leipzig University (~1837–1851) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1853–1874).

Moriz Winternitz was an Indologist who studied at the University of Vienna under Georg Bühler and under Friedrich Max Müller. He held professorships at the German University in Prague (~1899–1934) and a visiting professorship at Visva-Bharati University (1922–1923).

Morten Schlütter is a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar. He studied at Copenhagen, Komazawa, and Yale under Stanley Weinstein, and has held posts at Yale, Victoria University of Wellington, UCLA, the University of Wisconsin-Madison, and the University of Iowa.

Mortimer Wheeler was an archaeologist and Indologist educated at Bradford Grammar School and University College London. He held posts at Museum Wales, the London Museum, UCL Institute of Archaeology, and as Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India.

Morton Klass was a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at Brooklyn College and Columbia University. He held posts at the US Merchant Marine (1945), Bennington College (1959), Barnard College (1965), and Columbia University (1982–1985).
Mother Sayamagyi was a religious and Buddhist studies figure who was a disciple of Sayagyi U Ba Khin and eventually succeeded him.
Motohiro Yoritomi was a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at Kyoto University under Gadjin Nagao and Yuichi Kajiyama (~1968–1974). He became a professor at Shuchiin University in 1975.

Motoi Ono is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied under Yasunori Ejima, attended the University of Tsukuba, earned a doctorate at the University of Vienna, and served as an associate professor at Tsukuba (~1994–2023).
Motoichi Miyamoto is a scholar in Indology and philosophy who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1968–1978) and served as an assistant professor at Kokugakuin University (~1984–1993).

Mrinalkanti Gangopadhyaya is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He held teaching posts at Vidyasagar College (attested between 1970 and 1990) and in the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta (attested 1982 and 1994).
